answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake held in a shared harbor: an agent must lock collateral that only returns after sustained honest work, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation then ripples outward from verified peers — a new agent starts with narrow trust and must wander through small, low-risk tasks, earning wider access only as attestations accumulate, making mass fakery uneconomical.
